standard.title: Develop language for classroom exchanges
standard.description: develop language to interact in exchanges, routines, tasks and responsibilities related to classroom and interests
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can exchange basic personal information in familiar contexts using modelled language (AC9LS8EC01). They have not yet developed the functional classroom language needed to participate in the routines, tasks and responsibilities of the target language learning environment.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interact in the target language to manage classroom routines, ask for help or permission, follow and give instructions, express opinions and participate in classroom tasks and collaborative activities.

nodes.label: Following and giving classroom instructions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can follow modelled instructions and commands in the target language and attempt to give simple instructions to peers.
nodes.minimum_width: Follow at least four common classroom commands in the target language reliably; attempt to give one or two simple instructions.
nodes.typical_width: Follow and give a range of classroom instructions (open/close, listen, write, read, work with a partner); respond appropriately to teacher commands during regular classroom routines.
wider: Lead a class activity segment using only target language instructions — managing transitions and turn-taking
Create a bilingual classroom reference resource (poster, card set) translating common commands between the target language and English
nodes.hinge_reason: Classroom instruction language is the operational medium of the language classroom. Students who cannot follow basic commands cannot access the task structures through which all subsequent language learning occurs. This is a functional floor, not an enrichment item.

response_modes.reason: Reliable response to instructions requires automaticity — students need repeated encounters with the same commands in varied classroom routines until response becomes habitual rather than effortful.

success_criteria: Responds correctly to at least four common classroom commands in the target language without translation support
Can give at least one simple instruction to a peer in the target language

nodes.label: Asking for help, information and permission
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use modelled phrases to ask for help, clarification or permission in the target language.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two modelled phrases for asking for help or permission in a classroom context.
nodes.typical_width: Use a set of modelled phrases to ask for help, check understanding, request repetition, ask for information or seek permission; distinguish appropriately between formal and informal forms of address when making requests.
wider: Extend asking strategies to unfamiliar contexts — e.g. a simulated phone call, an email to a teacher, or a transaction scenario
Develop a personal 'survival phrase' card listing key asking strategies and add to it across the unit

response_modes.reason: Students need a bank of asking strategies rather than one memorised phrase. Exposure to multiple modelled forms across varied asking scenarios builds the flexibility needed to manage breakdowns in communication.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Asking strategies are directly linked to communication repair and intercultural survival skills developed in EC05. Building a rich repertoire now creates transferable tools the student will use beyond the classroom.
success_criteria: Can produce at least two contextually appropriate asking phrases in the target language without prompting
Can distinguish between formal and informal address when making a request

nodes.label: Expressing opinions and reactions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can express simple opinions and reactions using set phrases in the target language.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two modelled set phrases to express agreement, disagreement or a simple opinion in a classroom context.
nodes.typical_width: Use a range of set phrases to express opinions, reactions and thoughts; respond to others' opinions with agreement or simple contrast; use spontaneous interjections and expressions to maintain simple interactions.
wider: Participate in a structured classroom debate or 'four corners' opinion activity using target language opinion phrases
Collect and compare opinion expressions across different registers — identify which are appropriate in which social contexts

response_modes.reason: Opinion expression at Y7-8 entry is phrase-dependent — students need a bank of set expressions before they can participate authentically in opinion exchanges. Varied low-stakes opinion tasks build this bank.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Opinion phrases are the building blocks for the substantive discussion and argument structures required in AC9LS10EC02 (Y9-10). Rich repertoire now prevents students from being limited to 'I like/I don't like' at secondary level.
success_criteria: Can use at least two different opinion phrases in the target language in a classroom exchange
Can respond to a peer's opinion with agreement or a simple contrasting phrase

nodes.label: Participating in collaborative tasks and activities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can participate in collaborative classroom tasks and games using target language for sharing, encouraging, taking turns and completing joint activities.
nodes.minimum_width: Complete one collaborative classroom task using target language for at least one functional purpose (e.g. taking turns, asking a partner for information).
nodes.typical_width: Participate in games, paired activities and group tasks using target language to share, praise, encourage and coordinate; use classroom instruction language to manage the activity.
wider: Design and facilitate a simple classroom game that requires participants to use target language throughout (not just as a trigger for an English activity)
Facilitate a class routine (roll call, task distribution, instructions to peers) using only target language

response_modes.reason: Collaborative tasks are where instructions, asking strategies and opinion phrases from nodes 1–3 operate simultaneously. The teaching investment is in creating task structures where students must draw on multiple functional language sets at once.

success_criteria: Uses at least one functional target language phrase (instruction, asking, opinion) spontaneously during a collaborative task — not only in a scripted exchange
Can complete a paired or group activity with the target language as the primary medium of interaction
